chunks: Scripting and automation in ECAD. The question: Do you have any scripting experience in ECAD?
Scripting means writing a small program that does repetitive board-design work for you, such as placing parts in a pattern or checking a parts list.
The interviewer wants to hear that you have automated something real and that you do it carefully.
If you have not, an honest answer plus a similar example (like a short Python program that reads a parts list) is fine.
Imagine drawing the twelve numbers around a clock face by hand. They would come out uneven.
A rule such as "put one number every 30 degrees around the circle" gives a perfect result every time, and the same rule handles sixty marks as easily as twelve.
A script is that rule, written so the computer applies it.
The first decision is whether the task is worth automating at all.
The second splits scripts into safe (read exported files) and risky (edit the live design), which determines how careful you must be.
Script: a short program that automates a task. API: the set of commands a design tool lets your code use to read and change the design.
BOM (bill of materials): the list of parts to buy. MPN (manufacturer part number): the maker's exact code for a part.
Export: a plain file (such as a CSV table) saved out of the tool. A script that only reads exports cannot damage your design.
Place 12 LEDs in a ring of radius 20 mm. Each LED goes 360° ÷ 12 = 30° further around the circle. The first sits at (20, 0) mm, the next at about (17. 3, 10) mm, and so on.
Neighbors end up about 10. 4 mm apart. A short loop does this exactly; by hand it is slow and uneven.
A safe second script reads the exported parts list and flags any line with no part number. In the interview, fill in your own version: "I wrote [script] in [tool] to [task] .
I ran it on a copy and checked the result with [DRC or a review] ." That is the whole idea.
"My scripting is [level] . I've done [e. g.
a KiCad Python script that places LEDs on a circle using x = cx + r cos θ, y = cy + r sin θ, and a BOM checker in Python that groups lines and flags missing part numbers] .
The other tools have hooks too: Altium scripting and API, Eagle ULPs, Allegro SKILL.
I'd run any editing script on a copy, check with DRC, and keep it in version control so releases are repeatable."
